newsitem.title: USA: EMLICO talks focus on reinsurance, deal nears.
newsitem.headline: EMLICO talks focus on reinsurance, deal nears.

text.p: Massachusetts regulators are negotiating a settlement with General Electric Co that would subject its insolvent liability insurer EMLICO to U.S. laws on reinsurance issues while keeping the company in Bermuda, people familiar with the talks said.
Although the talks are still ongoing, a deal may be reached within the next few days, a source said.
Such a deal would be important because GE, the insurer's sole creditor and policyholder, might recover less from reinsurers under the U.S. laws.

The insurer, Electric Mutual Liability Insurance Co (EMLICO), relocated to Bermuda from Beverly, Mass., in June 1995 and then, faced with massive environmental claims, declared insolvency four months later.
EMLICO's reinsurers have claimed that regulators were misled into approving the redomestication so that General Electric could take advantage of the island's liquidation laws.
Under Bermuda liquidation laws, General Electric would have more say in the proceedings and the reinsurers would be likely to owe GE much greater sums than under the U.S. laws.
General Electric was not immediately available for comment. But the company has previously charged the reinsurers were just trying to avoid paying their bills.

Although the reinsurers, including Kemper Reinsurance Co, General Re Corp, and Lloyd's of London, have been seeking to return EMLICO to Massachusetts, a deal that would liquidate EMLICO under U.S. law would address one of their key concerns.
The Massachusetts insurance department confirmed it was in settlement talks with General Electric, EMLICO and Electric Insurance Co, a subsidiary of EMLICO.
But, the department declined comment on the content of the talks.

Another one of EMLICO's reinsurers, Allstate Corp, on Friday said it had reached a settlement with the joint liquidators of EMLICO and GE concerning insurance and reinsurance contracts between the companies.
As part of the settlement, all legal action between the parties will be dismissed.
The settlement was approved by the Supreme Court of Bermuda. Terms and conditions were not disclosed.
